nib1.intro: The Rubinstein: White plays the e-pawn and a bishop to d3, and Black builds with pawns on d5 and c5 and a knight on c6.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and watches the centre. Black does not commit a central pawn yet.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
e6 frees the dark-squared bishop and supports a central pawn.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
Bb4 pins the knight on c3 to the king on e1. This pin is the Nimzo-Indian.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop. Accepting the pin is the Rubinstein.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims towards the kingside.
d5 claims a share of the centre and attacks the pawn on c4.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
c5 attacks the pawn on d4 and challenges the centre.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king steps off the pin.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and adds pressure to the pawn on d4.

nib2.intro: The Rubinstein with an isolated pawn: Black takes on c4 and d4, and White takes back with the e-pawn.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls e4.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
e6 frees the dark-squared bishop and supports a central pawn.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
Bb4 pins the knight on c3 to the king on e1.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims towards the kingside.
d5 claims a share of the centre and attacks the pawn on c4.
Nf3 develops the king's knight.
c5 attacks the pawn on d4.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king steps off the pin.
dxc4 takes the pawn on c4 and opens the position.
Bxc4 recaptures the pawn on c4. The light-squared bishop stays active.
cxd4 takes the pawn on d4 and opens the centre.
exd4 recaptures the pawn on d4. The d-pawn is isolated, and the lines are open.

nib3.intro: The Huebner: Black trades on c3, doubles the pawns, and closes the centre with the e-pawn.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and watches the centre.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
e6 frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
Bb4 pins the knight on c3 to the king on e1.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
c5 attacks the pawn on d4. Black challenges the centre before castling.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims towards the kingside.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d4.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
Bxc3+ takes the knight on c3 and gives check. Black doubles the pawns on purpose.
bxc3 recaptures the bishop on c3. The c-pawns are doubled, and White has the bishop pair.
d6 supports the centre and keeps the position flexible.
e4 claims the centre. The doubled pawns are the cost of this space.
e5 closes the centre. The light-squared bishop on d3 is blocked by the pawn on e4.

nib4.intro: A Rubinstein where White avoids doubled pawns. The knight comes to e2, the a-pawn asks the bishop to move, and the bishop drops back.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls e4.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
e6 frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
Bb4 pins the knight on c3 to the king on e1.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Ne2 develops the king's knight where it can recapture on c3. White is avoiding doubled pawns.
d5 claims a share of the centre and attacks the pawn on c4.
a3 asks the bishop on b4 a question.
Be7 steps the bishop back. Black declines the trade, so White keeps a healthy pawn structure.

nib5.intro: The Classical: the queen comes to c2 so she can take back on c3, and Black prepares a fianchetto.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls e4.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
e6 frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
Bb4 pins the knight on c3 to the king on e1.
Qc2 develops the queen and defends the knight on c3. She is also ready to recapture there, so the pawns need not double.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
a3 asks the bishop on b4 a question.
Bxc3+ takes the knight on c3 and gives check.
Qxc3 recaptures the bishop on c3. The queen takes, and the pawns stay healthy.
b6 prepares the fianchetto. The light-squared bishop wants the long diagonal.

nib6.intro: The Classical with an immediate strike in the centre. Pawns come off on d5, the bishop pins from g5, and Black plays the c-pawn.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls e4.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
e6 frees the dark-squared bishop and supports the central pawn that follows.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
Bb4 pins the knight on c3 to the king on e1.
Qc2 develops the queen and defends the knight on c3.
d5 claims the centre and attacks the pawn on c4.
cxd5 takes the pawn on d5 and opens the c-file.
exd5 recaptures the pawn on d5 and opens the e-file.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8.
h6 asks the bishop on g5 a question.
Bh4 keeps the dark-squared bishop on the pinning diagonal and steps off the pawn.
c5 attacks the pawn on d4 and challenges the centre.

nib7.intro: The Saemisch: White forces the trade on c3 at once and accepts doubled pawns in return for the bishop pair.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls e4.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
e6 frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
Bb4 pins the knight on c3 to the king on e1.
a3 asks the bishop on b4 a question at once. White wants the trade now.
Bxc3+ takes the knight on c3 and gives check.
bxc3 recaptures the bishop on c3. The pawns are doubled, and White keeps the bishop pair.
c5 attacks the pawn on d4 and puts pressure on the doubled pawns.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d4.
Bd3 develops the light-squared bishop and aims towards the kingside.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8.
Ne2 develops the king's knight. The c-pawn sits on c3, so this knight uses e2.
d6 supports the centre and keeps the position solid.

nib8.intro: The Kmoch with the f-pawn on f3: Black strikes in the centre before White can settle the doubled pawns.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls e4.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
e6 frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
Bb4 pins the knight on c3 to the king on e1.
f3 supports a central pawn and takes e4 under firmer control. The king's knight will not develop to its usual square.
d5 strikes at the centre before White consolidates.
a3 asks the bishop on b4 a question.
Bxc3+ takes the knight on c3 and gives check.
bxc3 recaptures the bishop on c3. The pawns are doubled.
c5 attacks the pawn on d4 and increases the pressure on the doubled pawns.

nib9.intro: The Leningrad: the bishop pins from g5, Black challenges with the c-pawn, and White pushes the d-pawn.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls e4.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
e6 frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
Bb4 pins the knight on c3 to the king on e1.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8. White answers the pin with a pin.
h6 asks the bishop on g5 a question.
Bh4 keeps the dark-squared bishop on the pinning diagonal and steps off the pawn.
c5 attacks the pawn on d4 and challenges the centre.
d5 gains a wedge of space and attacks the pawn on e6.
d6 supports the centre and keeps the wedge from becoming a target on its own.

nib10.intro: A Three Knights move order that reaches a Ragozin. Black kicks the bishop with the g-pawn and plants a knight on e4.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and controls e4.
c4 gains space and fights for the centre.
e6 frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and fights for the centre.
Bb4 pins the knight on c3 to the king on e1.
Nf3 develops the king's knight. White does not pin the knight on f6 yet.
d5 claims the centre and attacks the pawn on c4.
cxd5 takes the pawn on d5.
exd5 recaptures the pawn on d5 and opens the e-file.
Bg5 pins the knight on f6 to the queen on d8.
h6 asks the dark-squared bishop a question.
Bh4 keeps the pin and steps off the pawn.
g5 attacks the bishop on h4 and gains kingside space.
Bg3 drops the dark-squared bishop back and keeps it on the board.
Ne4 plants the knight in the centre and attacks the bishop on g3.
